l4Discriminating.text: Readings are pseudorandom, synthetic, or not coupled to real physical phenomena (e.g., test data, simulation, or instrument firmware generating simulated output) — Pseudorandom or simulated data would naturally show near-zero correlations across all lags and between channels, while maintaining realistic marginal distributions and spacing. The pattern of zero autocorrelations, zero cross-correlations, realistic variance, and no exact runs is almost a signature of high-quality synthetic data. However, this hypothesis requires that I am either reviewing test data by mistake or that the instruments are not actually connected to physical apparatus. My *meticulous baseline protocol*—establishing baselines from day 1, checking calibration—is inconsistent with running unknowingly on synthetic data. A colleague or setup error could have substituted simulated output, but I would expect to find evidence of this during calibration checks or when comparing instrument readings to independently measured physical quantities.

l4Discriminating.text: Readings are synthetic or test data, generated with independent noise streams — High-quality synthetic data with independent noise generators for each channel would show exactly this signature: near-zero autocorrelations, near-zero cross-correlations, realistic marginal distributions, appropriate variance, no exact runs. If instruments are running in simulation or test mode, or if a colleague substituted synthetic output without my knowledge, the data would be mathematically indistinguishable from what I observe. However, this requires either (a) me to be reviewing test data unknowingly, or (b) a colleague to have reconfigured instruments to output simulated rather than real data. My baseline procedure (days 1–10 with explicit calibration and n=88–100 per instrument) would normally trigger questions if I was unaware of running on test data, e.g., 'why are there no correlations?' or 'what is this connected to?' I have not recorded such questions in my notebook, suggesting I believed the data was real. A colleague could have substituted output, but I would expect to find evidence during any independent cross-checks or physical observations of the apparatus.
